description.en: Zambia observes a range of public holidays reflecting its national history, culture, and traditions. These holidays affect work schedules, school terms, and travel plans across the country.

sections.title: About Zambia
sections.content: Zambia, officially the Republic of Zambia, is a landlocked country in Southern Africa. It is bordered to the north by the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Tanzania to the northeast, Malawi to the east, Mozambique to the southeast, Zimbabwe and Botswana to the south, Namibia to the southwest, and Angola to the west. The capital city of Zambia is Lusaka, located in the south-central part of Zambia. The population is concentrated mainly around Lusaka in the south and the Copperbelt Province to the north, the core economic hubs of Zambia.

sections.title: Important Notice
sections.content: Public holiday dates and observance rules can change, especially when holidays fall on weekends. Always confirm critical dates with official Zambia government sources when planning travel, payroll, or business operations.

sections.title: How Zambia's Public Holidays Are Observed
sections.content:
On most public and bank holidays:

Banks and government offices are closed.
Schools are closed.
Some businesses operate reduced hours.
Public transport and retail services may run modified schedules.
Private businesses are not legally required to close but often adjust operating hours.

sections.title: Why Zambia's Public Holidays Matter
sections.content:
Understanding Zambia's public holidays helps with:

Business and payroll planning.
School and academic scheduling.
Travel and accommodation planning.
Avoiding service disruptions.
Both residents and visitors benefit from knowing when closures and peak travel periods are likely.

q.en: Are all public holidays observed nationwide in Zambia?

a.en: While many holidays are national, some observances may be limited to specific regions, states, or territories.

q.en: Do businesses and stores close on public holidays in Zambia?

a.en: Generally yes. Government offices, banks, and schools are closed. Essential services and some retail sectors may remain open or operate on reduced hours.

q.en: What happens if a public holiday falls on a weekend in Zambia?

a.en: In many cases, if a national holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the observance is moved to the following Monday, though this depends on specific local laws and the holiday in question.

q.en: Are public transport services affected by holidays in Zambia?

a.en: Yes, public transportation often runs on a reduced Sunday or holiday schedule during national public holidays.

q.en: Are employees entitled to paid time off on public holidays in Zambia?

a.en: Most full-time employees are legally entitled to a paid day off on national public holidays. Those who are required to work are typically eligible for premium pay or a substitute day off.
